reviewContext.userProblem: riela has no bot or agent-identity record, so nothing answers what each agent is doing right now. The gateway adapter drops most ACP session updates (plan, usage, config, commands, sub-agents, terminal updates) and declines every permission request unseen; model names are free strings; riela memory is not scoped to an agent; a riela client cannot pair with a riela server and drive its bots.
requiredOutcomes: Slice a: a persisted, runtime-store-owned bot record with runtime-owned linkage to sessions, routines and Work tasks; overview and task board (Needs you, In progress, Waiting, Planned, Closed) on CLI `riela bot`, GraphQL and web, derived from runtime records.

Slice b: every ACP v1/v2 session update, permission request and stop reason normalised into one typed, backend-neutral, bounded, persisted activity stream with live long-poll and replay; answerable permission requests with option ids passed through; deterministic settlement on every terminal path; non-ACP backends report an explicit activitySource.

Slice c: runtime-owned provider-instance and model catalog (bundled manifest merged with backend-reported models, custom models, `default` sentinel never sent, passive probes); `riela model`, `riela provider`, GraphQL and web; unknown models warn instead of failing.
Slice d: server-owned list state (pin, manual order, snooze, settle, Working group, return-to-top, `limited` status, grouping) rendered identically by CLI, GraphQL and web.

Slice e: per-bot riela memory in the existing RielaMemoryStore (memory id bot-<botId>, no schema change), Markdown read/edit/export, audited change sets with list, diff and undo, prompt injection inside the overflow guard budget, write rules enforced by the runtime.

Slice f: memory upkeep job (text-only reply applied by the runtime), look-around job that is read-only by sandbox and tool policy, suggestions that need acceptance, feedback captured as memory candidates through the same audited path.

Slice g: `riela serve` pairing with one-time expiring codes, hashed scoped revocable grants on RielaAPIKeyStore, audit records, `riela remote` client registry under the credential-dir convention, forwarding with origin identity, disconnected state never reported as idle.

Deterministic tests for normalisation, status derivation, memory scoping and undo, look-around read-only enforcement, pairing expiry, reuse, revocation and scope; parity gates and generated SDL green; mock-scenario example bundle `bot-routine-memory-upkeep` registered.
nonGoals: A relay or cloud service, a new transport (SSE, WebSocket, GraphQL subscription) or a new auth system.
Changing how workflows, routines, Work tasks or sessions execute; a bot adds no scheduler and no dispatcher.
Bot default backend or model overriding a workflow node's own settings.
Vendoring or patching agent-gateway, or changing Package.swift pins.
kaiba long-term knowledge; bot memory is riela memory only.
Scripted activity in mock scenarios; mock runs report activitySource: session.
Queuing requests for an unreachable server; such a request fails with remote_unreachable.
constraints: Base on branch tip 7f04f6e6 (includes ACP v2); do not reintroduce pre-ACP-v2 code paths.
Runtime records are owned by the runtime store, never by workers or adapters; behaviour stays deterministic.
No backward-compatibility shims for unreleased shapes; never break or bump existing user memory databases; no edit of Packages/RielaMemory.
No worktree, branch, stash, commit or push by implementers; gitPush is false; per-edit SHA-256 and drift rules in impl-plans/active/bots-overview.md section 2.
Swift commands run as arch -arm64 /bin/zsh -lc '<command>' in the foreground with full logs under tmp/bots-overview/<planId>.
Tests never touch ~/.riela or the real credential directory; isolated roots only.
Scratch files only under tmp/bots-overview; nothing at the repository root or in scripts/.
Do not change Package.swift, Package.resolved, VERSION or anything under .build.
English-only, low-text web UI following existing SolidJS conventions; web/package.json and web/bun.lock stay unchanged (bun install --frozen-lockfile).
Earlier slices must work without later ones; if the run stops early, accepted waves are complete slices and the remaining plans stay active.
Each wave gate runs the cumulative filter C<n> of impl-plans/active/bots-overview.md section 4; the final gate is section 5.

designDecisionsAndRationale.decision: A bot is a thin record in the session store database (generation 13, additive tables) over existing routines, sessions, Work tasks and riela memory.
designDecisionsAndRationale.rationale: Design sections 4 and 5: reuse existing records; add storage only where no existing record can answer the question.

designDecisionsAndRationale.decision: One pure projector produces the board, overview row and ordered list for CLI, GraphQL and web.
designDecisionsAndRationale.rationale: Design sections 5.3, 5.4 and 8: all surfaces render the same server-derived output, so they stay identical.

designDecisionsAndRationale.decision: Activity events, the state row and settlement are written in one transaction by a bounded recorder fed from the runner's adapter call site; live and replay use one cursor-paged long-poll read.
designDecisionsAndRationale.rationale: Design sections 6.3 to 6.7: deterministic reducer, bounded replay window, no new transport.

designDecisionsAndRationale.decision: Permission requests become runtime-owned pending records with a bounded wait and a deterministic default on timeout; GatewayClientPermissionResponder(policy: .cancel) is removed.
designDecisionsAndRationale.rationale: Design section 6.6: native option ids pass through unchanged and every request can be declined.

designDecisionsAndRationale.decision: Rich ACP activity is tested with scripted ACP agents and Swift string fixtures; the required agent-gateway change is recorded as an upstream follow-up.
designDecisionsAndRationale.rationale: Design section 15: the pinned in-process agent emits only message and thought chunks; the dependency is not vendored or patched.

designDecisionsAndRationale.decision: Bot memory uses the existing RielaMemoryStore with memory id bot-<botId>; every write goes through one audited writer with a redact closure.
designDecisionsAndRationale.rationale: Design section 9: no schema bump for user memory databases; RielaCore cannot import RielaWork.

designDecisionsAndRationale.decision: Look-around is forced read-only by the runner (forceReadOnlySandbox) and a policy check, not only by prompt.
designDecisionsAndRationale.rationale: Design section 10.2 and the acceptance criterion on enforcement.

designDecisionsAndRationale.decision: Pairing extends RielaAPIKeyStore with scoped grants; the client command family is named `riela remote`.
designDecisionsAndRationale.rationale: Design section 11: reuse API-key machinery; `riela environment` already means workflow instance environment.

designDecisionsAndRationale.rationale: impl-plans/active/bots-overview.md section 3: the provider must start workflow runs.

intentionalTradeoffs: Ten serial waves trade wall-clock time for single ownership of shared registries.
The cumulative wave-gate filter grows to 93 suites, so later gates take longer.
Long-poll instead of SSE, WebSocket or subscriptions.
Event sourcing is applied to the activity log and its state row only; the runner is not re-architected.
Persona stays an existing personaId reference; no new Markdown file format for persona or skills.
An opaque pairing code string instead of a URL scheme.
supportedEdgeCases: Out-of-order tool_call_update, plan replacement and removal, permission request, cancellation.
Settlement on completion, cancel, provider error and process exit, including orphan reconcile and abandoned nested invocations.
Retention deletes a session's activity rows and bot link in the same transaction.
Usage or rate limit stop reported as `limited` with a reset time.
Paused or busy bot skips upkeep and look-around; missed runs catch up.
Snooze wakes early on needs-you or failure; auto-settle is blocked by in-progress or pending work.
Pairing code expiry, reuse, revocation dropping access at once, scope enforcement, refusal of loopback and wildcard addresses.
Missing origin identity is reported as unverifiable; an unreachable remote is shown as disconnected with last-known state.
Unknown model yields a model_unknown warning; the `default` sentinel is never sent to a provider.
bun install failure is recorded as BLOCKED: environment, never as a pass.
outOfScopeEdgeCases: Rich activity from the pinned in-process agent-gateway agent (upstream follow-up, design section 15).
Requests queued while a remote is unreachable.
Avatars and connector conversations as bot children.
TLS termination; a private-network path is a documented requirement.
Live audio, kaiba or other backends' long-term knowledge.
